Improvidence

im-PROV-i-dents · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Improvidence is carelessness or lack of foresight, especially with money.

The financial counselor blamed the family's debt on years of improvidence -- spending every paycheck the moment it arrived with no plan for emergencies.

Worked Example

His improvidence in his twenties -- never once opening a savings account -- left him with nothing to fall back on when he lost his job at forty.

Improvidence names the habit itself: spending without any thought for tomorrow, not a single unlucky event.

How Improvidence Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

recklessness

recklessness: the everyday word for plunging into risk without a thought; improvidence is its formal cousin - failing to provide for the future

shortsightedness

shortsightedness: failure to plan for the future

Antonyms

thrift

thrift: careful management of money

foresight

foresight: the ability to plan ahead wisely

How Strong Is It? — carelessness → improvidence → improvidence

carelessness vs. improvidence

carelessness vs. improvidence: A little carelessness with a coupon is no big deal.

improvidence vs. improvidence

improvidence vs. improvidence: Real improvidence means blowing an entire paycheck with no plan for next month's rent.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — im-

prefix — im-: not (Latin)

root — providence

root — providence: foresight, seeing ahead (Latin (providere))

Put it together

Put it together: im- ("not") + providence ("foresight") = a lack of foresight, especially about money.

Use the root in a new word: provide

Use the root in a new word: provide: The same root survives in the everyday word "provide" -- literally, to see to someone's needs ahead of time.
